description:
A guard-selected clause's return type is joined across all callsites, because
integer-literal identity is erased before reachability analysis runs. Since spec
enforcement landed at user callsites, that widened type now makes ordinary code a
COMPILE ERROR, not merely an imprecise type.

## Repro (prebuilt target/debug/fz2, verified twice)

    fn pick({:ok, x}) when x > 0, do: x
    fn pick({:ok, _}), do: :fallback
    fn main() do
      dbg(pick({:ok, 1}))
      dbg(pick({:ok, 0}))
      dbg(pick({:ok, 1}) + 1)
    end

    error[spec/violation]: call to `+/2` violates its @spec for arguments (int | :fallback, int)
      --> guard2.fz:6:7
     6 |   dbg(pick({:ok, 1}) + 1)
       |       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ no declared @spec accepts these arguments

ELIXIR ACCEPTS IT. The same shape under a module prints `1`, `:fallback`, `2`.

Drop the third `dbg` and both interp and run print `1` then `:fallback` -- the
runtime VALUES are correct. The defect is entirely in the static return type.

## Atom control, which still passes

    fn pick2(:a), do: 1
    fn pick2(_), do: :fallback
    dbg(pick2(:a) + 1)      => 2

Atom singletons survive into the lattice and mint distinct activations, so
narrowing works there. Integer literals do not. That contrast is the whole bug.

## Root cause, re-verified at HEAD

`ActivationKey::from_inputs` (src/compiler2/identity.rs:98) keys purely on
argument `Ty` via `types.address_inputs(inputs)`. `Types::int_lit`
(src/compiler2/types/mod.rs:389) collapses every numeric literal to plain `int`,
with the documented rationale "Numeric literals are VALUES, not types: the
lattice deliberately cannot express a numeric singleton". `as_int_singleton`
(:1125) is a permanent `None` stub.

So `pick({:ok, 1})` and `pick({:ok, 0})` mint the IDENTICAL `ActivationKey`,
share one `reachable_clause_ids` computation and one joined `ReturnType` fact
that both callsites read. `Region::Guard` correctly answers "both branches
possible" for what looks to it like a genuinely polymorphic activation; literal
identity was erased before reachability ever ran.

## Why this is not a point fix

It needs a literal-value channel independent of `Ty` -- either per-callsite guard
re-evaluation against the caller's own literal operands, or carrying literal
values in the `ActivationKey` / dispatch input alongside the erased `Ty`. That is
a deliberate change to the activation-identity model, and it is the numeric
analogue of what atom singletons already get. `GroundValue` (fz-yj0) now exists
and is the natural carrier.

## Checks

- The repro above compiles and prints `1`, `:fallback`, `2` on interp, run and
  build.
- Fill the assertion currently marked NOT FILLED in
  `guard_partition_selects_refined_clause` (src/compiler2/port_type_infer_test.rs:1288)
  to `{int, :fallback}`; the root-cause trace is in the TODO at :1298-1323.
- `direct_calls_specialize_atom_pattern_dispatch_by_input` stays green.
- Promote `fixtures2/00206_match_guard_clause.fz` or
  `fixtures2/00401_guard_partition.fz` into fixtures2/behavior with an oracle --
  neither is in the matrix today, so nothing guards this.

## What the old ticket got wrong

Line refs drifted: `int_lit` is types/mod.rs:389 (was cited as :360),
`as_int_singleton` is :1125 (was :980). `guard_partition_selects_refined_clause`
is a TEST name, not a fixture. And the impact statement predates spec
enforcement: the consequence is no longer an over-wide inferred type, it is a
fatal `error[spec/violation]` on code Elixir accepts.
title: Guard-clause dispatch does not narrow return type per-callsite, and the widened type now fatally fails @spec enforcement on valid code
